summary: Add OpenTelemetry tracing and metrics to the only running service in the repo, tools/warehouse-server (Fastify and built-in SQLite). Export over OTLP, configured through standard OTEL_* environment variables, and disabled by default so existing behaviour and tests are unchanged.
approach: The issue is one line with no scope. The repo has one runtime service: the Fastify API in tools/warehouse-server. The Java domain model is a plain library with no process to instrument, and sales-orders-ui is a standalone browser app, so this plan scopes to the server. Add the OpenTelemetry Node SDK as a small, separate bootstrap module that registers tracer and meter providers with a service.name resource and an OTLP exporter, and starts only when enabled by configuration. It must load before Fastify and node:http are imported; because the package is ESM running under tsx, preload it with Node's --import flag in the dev and start scripts rather than importing it from index.ts. HTTP and Fastify instrumentations then give a span per request with route, method and status, plus standard HTTP server metrics. node:sqlite has no auto-instrumentation, so database spans are optional and kept minimal. The OTLP endpoint comes only from OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT with no hardcoded default; non-local endpoints must use HTTPS; auth headers come from OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS and are never committed or logged. Telemetry is off unless configured, and shutdown flushes pending data. Existing tests build the app through buildApp and must not need a collector.

alternatives_considered.option: Instrument the Java domain model in src/main/java
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It is a dependency-free library with no runtime, no build tool and no process. Adding the OpenTelemetry Java API would break the repo's no-dependency javac harness.

alternatives_considered.option: Add browser instrumentation to warehouse-ui and sales-orders-ui
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The issue gives no signal that frontend telemetry is wanted. It adds bundle weight and needs CORS and collector exposure. It can be a follow-up.

alternatives_considered.option: Manual spans only, with no auto-instrumentation
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: More code to maintain, and it misses the standard HTTP semantic conventions.

alternatives_considered.option: Import the SDK at the top of index.ts instead of preloading
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Under ESM the HTTP and Fastify modules would already be loaded, so auto-instrumentation would silently not patch them.

alternatives_considered.option: Always-on telemetry with a default collector endpoint
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It would add startup noise and failed export attempts for developers and CI, and a default endpoint is a hardcoded network target.
OTLP is vendor-neutral, and the issue names OpenTelemetry.

components: tools/warehouse-server telemetry bootstrap (new): configures the Node SDK, resource attributes, OTLP trace and metric exporters, HTTP and Fastify instrumentations, enable/disable switch and shutdown flush
tools/warehouse-server start-up scripts and package.json: add OpenTelemetry dependencies and preload the bootstrap in dev and start
tools/warehouse-server/src/index.ts: flush and shut down telemetry on process exit, with no change to routes or response bodies
tools/warehouse-server/src/app.ts: expected to need no change because auto-instrumentation attaches externally; a small change only if span error status or route naming needs help
tools/warehouse-server tests (new): telemetry off by default, spans produced for API requests when enabled (in-memory exporter), existing suites unchanged
Root package-lock.json and workspace install: new dependencies resolved at the workspace root
Documentation (new section): OTEL_* variables, local collector usage and how to turn telemetry on
src/main/java, sales-orders-ui, tools/warehouse-ui, tools/bob-pipeline: read only, no changes
assumptions: "This project" means the runnable service, tools/warehouse-server. The Java library and the frontends are out of scope.
Traces and metrics are wanted. Logs signal export is not required, because the server uses Fastify's own logger.
OTLP is the export protocol. An OTLP-compatible collector or backend exists outside this repo, and no collector is bundled here.
Telemetry is opt-in through environment configuration, in line with the existing environment-driven settings (PORT, LOG_LEVEL, WAREHOUSE_DATA_DIR).
Node 22.13 or later (the current engine requirement) is compatible with the current OpenTelemetry JS SDK.
The server keeps binding to 127.0.0.1, and telemetry adds no new listening ports.

risks.risk: The issue is under-specified, so the intended scope (server only, frontends, Java) may differ from this plan
risks.mitigation: State the scope assumption explicitly and raise it in the open questions before implementation

risks.risk: ESM and tsx can stop auto-instrumentation from patching modules if the SDK loads too late
risks.mitigation: Preload the bootstrap with --import in all start scripts and test that spans are produced through the real server entry path

risks.risk: The OpenTelemetry JS packages move quickly and have separate experimental and stable version lines, so versions may be mismatched
risks.mitigation: Use matching current releases, pin them via the lock file, and verify with a spans test

risks.risk: The exporter adds overhead or fails when the collector is down
risks.mitigation: Use batch processors with bounded timeouts, opt-in enablement, and a test with an unreachable endpoint

risks.risk: Telemetry leaks sensitive data (headers, credentials, VINs, query strings)
risks.mitigation: Rely on default semantic-convention attributes only, never log exporter headers, and add an assertion test on span attributes

risks.risk: The node:sqlite driver has no auto-instrumentation, so database time is invisible
risks.mitigation: Accept for the first iteration, or add a thin manual span around WarehouseDb as a follow-up

risks.risk: New dependencies enlarge the workspace install and the lock file
risks.mitigation: Add dependencies only to tools/warehouse-server and keep them limited to the SDK, OTLP exporters and the two instrumentations

acceptance_criteria.criterion: With no OTEL_* configuration, the server starts and serves requests exactly as before, makes no network calls to any collector, and logs no telemetry errors.

When telemetry is enabled by configuration, each request to an /api/vehicles route produces a trace span with HTTP method, route and status code, under a configurable service.name (default warehouse-server).
HTTP server request metrics, such as request count and duration, are recorded and exported when telemetry is enabled.
A request that ends in a 5xx response produces a span with error status. A 4xx response (validation, 404, 409) is not marked as a server error.

The export endpoint, protocol, headers and sampling are set only through standard OTEL_* environment variables. No endpoint, credential or token is hardcoded or committed, and header values are never logged.
Non-local OTLP endpoints must use HTTPS. Exporter timeouts are bounded, so an unreachable collector cannot hang requests or shutdown.
If the collector is unreachable, API responses and latency are unaffected, and the server does not crash.
On normal termination the server flushes pending telemetry and shuts the SDK down.
The telemetry bootstrap loads before Fastify and the HTTP module in both npm run dev and npm run start, so auto-instrumentation takes effect.
Request bodies, query strings containing user data, and VIN values are not added to span attributes beyond default HTTP semantic conventions.

Existing tools/warehouse-server tests, typecheck, and root npm run test:warehouse and npm run typecheck pass with no new warnings. New tests cover the default-off behaviour and span creation using an in-memory exporter and no network.
Documentation lists the supported environment variables and how to try it against a local collector.
New dependencies are the latest stable, actively maintained OpenTelemetry packages, are pinned through the lock file, and have no known high or critical vulnerabilities.

open_questions: Is the scope the warehouse server only, or should the browser UIs and the Java model also be instrumented?
Which backend or collector will receive the data (for example an OpenTelemetry Collector, Jaeger or a vendor)? This affects the protocol (HTTP or gRPC) and the documentation examples.
Are database spans around WarehouseDb operations wanted in this issue?
Are metrics wanted as well as traces, or traces only? This plan assumes both.
